tasks.task: Get the brief and align with the project lead
tasks.what: Understand the scope and the deliverable due date.
tasks.how:
Get the brief from the project lead and check it against the standard scope (Scope & Context tab).
Hold a kick-off call with the project lead: scope, deliverable due date.

tasks.what: Make sure your time on the project is planned.
tasks.how:
Check your staffing on Float.
Validate it with the project lead.

tasks.what: Make sure you have everything to start.
tasks.how: Confirm you have the template and the Excel working file.
tasks.output: Template and Excel file at hand

tasks.what: Immerse yourself in the brand.
tasks.how:
Go to the brand website, social media accounts and read articles for brands' news.
Ask ChatGPT for the latest brand news (buzz, bestsellers, pop-up stores).

tasks.what: A very quali study, but it needs a solid data base.
tasks.how: Build the query from the community's values and hashtags.
tasks.watch_out: To validate with your project lead

tasks.what: Collect TikTok content on the community.
tasks.how:
Either via Meltwater.
Or via our internal tool, using identified hashtags (brand hashtags, community hashtags and its values).

tasks.what: Collect content from the other platforms.
tasks.how: Crawl via Radarly through the query
tasks.output: Instagram, Reddit and Pinterest crawl output

tasks.what: Identify the actors, celebrities or influencers who best embody the community.
tasks.how:
List the muses :
Spot them directly in the data.
Draw on your own knowledge of the community.
Browse TikTok or Instagram, searching for the community’s values in the search bar.
Crawl their posts via Radarly with the query "author:".

tasks.what: Your project lead sees what has been launched and where it stands.
tasks.how: Fill in the shared Excel file step by step.
tasks.output: Shared Excel file up to date

tasks.what: Make the data ready for analysis.
tasks.how: Load the data in the Corpus Manager (see Corpus Manager methodology).

tasks.what: Get a first understanding of the corpus and start collecting material.
tasks.how:
Ask Claude or Gemini whether celebrities, restaurant names or brands come up repeatedly.
Take 2 hours to read the data and set aside relevant verbatims.
tasks.watch_out: Check names surfaced by Claude in the verbatims before using them.

tasks.what: Indicate the audience's socio-demographic profile and centers of interest.
tasks.how: In HypeAuditor, generate the audience analysis of the brand accounts (beauty, fashion, all).

tasks.what: 5 to 7 slide manifesto: who they are, their relationship to fashion or beauty, who they follow.
tasks.how:
To find influencers, several methods:
Ask ChatGPT directly.
Use HypeAuditor lookalikes or direclty on lookalikes suggestion on Instagram & TikTok.
Last resort: Traackr, using its AI tool directly.

tasks.what: Top platforms.
tasks.how: Via Meltwater or the ICC.

tasks.what: Tone of voice.
tasks.how: Analyst's perception, confirmed via ChatGPT or Claude. Run a sample of data or frequencies through Claude
tasks.watch_out: Ground the tone of voice in exact verbatims, not in ChatGPT's description.

tasks.what: Top topics (what they talk about most) and deep dive of the topics.
tasks.how:
To find the topics: look at the frequencies, send them to Claude to have a first rough ideas of first topics.
To quantify the topics: look at the facets, recreate queries if needed, based on how consumers talk (check verbatims + frequencies)
tasks.output: Top topics and deep dive slides

tasks.what: Activation ideas for the client.
tasks.how: Propose ideas to your project lead. Get inspiration from what other brands do and work well, what drives engagement and positivity

tasks.task: Check the deck before sending to the project lead
tasks.what: The deck is clean and client-ready.
tasks.how:
No duplicate verbatims.
Base 100 adds up to 100.
Same font everywhere.
Title = insight.
No comments or notes left at the bottom of the slides.
Good quality photos.

tasks.what: Keep the project team aligned throughout the toolkit.
tasks.how: Plan at least 2 to 3 review calls per week with the project team.

tasks.what: Anticipate the restitution.
tasks.how:
Confirm with the project lead whether you should attend.
Make sure you have the invitation.

tasks.what: Get feedback on your work.
tasks.how: After the restitution, ask the project lead for written feedback (plus a quick coffee or call if needed).

deck.title: Toolkit | Deck Structure
deck.description: Standard slide sequence of a toolkit deck (deep dive on one community), with the data each slide needs and when it is included.
rows: Country, timeframe, sources (platforms); query extract; conversation volume.
4 to 7 traits (e.g. identity, references, mindset, social life, rituals, relationship to each category in scope): headline, narrative, 2 to 3 verbatims with platform and market flags, visual.
Always (one slide per category in scope)
Values moodboard with 4 to 5 labelled values and a framing headline; verbatim on the lead value.
Generation split %, most represented professions, also represented.
Name, archetype tagline, handles with followers and ER per platform, why she embodies the community, verbatim, visuals.
Platform share of conversation (donut), role of the top 2 platforms with 4 to 5 behaviours each, verbatims.
Platform deep dive (x each key platform)
Role headline, top hashtags, post examples with verbatims.
How the community uses blogs, forums, Reddit; example threads.
Key temples IRL (x each temple family)
Temple families with visual and named venues per city.
Tone headline, narrative, signature expressions and verbatims.
Top words & hashtags cloud; top emojis by theme.
P5 What do they talk about
P5 What do they talk about
3 macro topics with share, sub-topics listed under each, visual per topic.
P5 What do they talk about
Topic navigation (repeat before each macro topic)
Top topics overview with the current macro topic highlighted.
P5 What do they talk about
Headline, narrative, verbatims, visuals; per sub-topic as relevant: muses or celebrity looks decoded, top brands, formats, notes or claims.
P5 What do they talk about
Share of community conversation on the client category; split by sub-category; reading per sub-category; claims to leverage.
P5 What do they talk about
Top brands, formats, top notes / ingredients, top products mentioned, verbatims.
Activation ideas for creative / comms teams, each with rationale and reference example.
Tribes ID card: share per market, affinity, platforms, generation, values, who are they, centers of interest, top brands, key temples, influencer.
Handle, followers, ER, description, verbatims, feed visuals.

glossary.definition: A consumer community identified in a tribes study, gathered by shared values, codes and interests. After the tribes study, the client selects 1 or 2 tribes to deep dive in a toolkit.
An actor, celebrity or influencer who best embodies the community. Muses' posts are crawled via Radarly with the query "author:".

An even more qualitative study, built around an ideal rather than necessarily a community with shared values. When it comes to Archetype studies, the question for brand is not so much “Who should buy this fragrance?”, but “Who does this fragrance represent?” Our role is to identify the different types of people who naturally embody that territory in today’s culture.
After a tribes study, a deep dive that gives the client more material on who that community is.
